summary: Nine days after it started, Vivek finally got into Lauryn's Facebook account on Aug 16 - and he did it without her Gmail login, by having her create and then delete a passkey so Facebook fell back to an SMS code. She celebrated it ('FINALLY', '🥳🥳') and it also recovered her second page with 200k+ followers. That is the first real forward motion on this account in two weeks. Everything after that stalled: from Aug 18 to Aug 21 Vivek's only explanation was that 'facebook server is down' and 'Facebook servers is cooked rn', and the week closed with the client posting exactly the same complaint she opened the escalation with - 'PAGE NOT RECOMMENDED' (Aug 20). Two things went the wrong way. First, the credential line was crossed a third time: on Aug 15 she said she had 'Talked to my Management' and they 'can't give out certain passwords', and Vivek still came back on Aug 16 offering to log into her Gmail over a screen share - the exact escalation last week's file flagged as the trust break. He also told her 'Ma'am that's on you completely'. Second, Derrek disappeared. She completed his Aug 13 instructions, reported back on Aug 15 and tagged him twice ('Kk @ofwizz chime in'); he sent zero messages all week. On money, Stephski kept her word and rolled the $1,852.15 into the Aug 15 invoice, but that invoice also carried yet another bank account change, quoted no amount and no due date, got no acknowledgment from the client, and was never followed up - six silent days on a bill that now contains three periods of carryover.

Holding the score down: the actual complaint is unchanged after 328 days - she ended the week typing 'PAGE NOT RECOMMENDED' again; Vivek asked for Gmail access a third time and told her a problem was 'on you completely'; he spent Aug 19 reporting on Instagram, which she had to correct ('My IG was never shadow banned'); Derrek went silent all week after she did exactly what he asked; and the Aug 15 invoice with a three-period carryover went out with a new account number, no stated amount or deadline, and no chase.
